methodology: Initial Node baseline, not a speed gate or universal performance claim. Current identical workload resolves historical/candidate source and export maps. Full C8 candidate and ordinary overlapping baseline profiles gate before timing; fixed edge cases are not timed against baseline failures. Native G7 outputs gate field-by-field against pinned stored controls at existing accuracy budgets. Solver setup consumes normalized area without retaining all constructed instances (JIT escape analysis may apply). Public direct calls (including line setup), and reused lines are separate jobs. All non-area geodesic outputs are requested on both sides; rhumb comparator is C++ Exact. Inputs, reusable buffers, solver/line preparation and correctness checks are outside operation timing. Warmup is three batches. Samples rotate baseline/candidate/native order; native process startup, I/O and preparation are excluded by its internal steady clock. Native processes warm one batch per sample; JS shares a process, so cross-language ratios remain diagnostic. Output dispatch/stores and public JS object costs are included. Heap sampling runs after all timings, includes runtime overhead and may miss allocations; zero samples do not establish zero allocation. No native heap claim. No browser throughput or new bulk-API claim.
